mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy accompanied by falling inflation, which may boost real interest rates and depress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of such joint events.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly for two months) combined with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month average signals a demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly growth for 2 months AND HOUST > 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS falling for three consecutive months) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes outside monetary easing periods.
